bluefin_recreational.narrative: First fish (giants) show mid-late April in NJ. Recreational-size arrive June, peak July-Aug (jig/pop bite mid-30 to 65 in). Sept still strong, giants return. October wanes at Coxes/S of Block.

bluefin_giant.narrative: Giants arrive first (Apr-May) and last (through Dec). Peak Nov in NJ/LI bunker migration. Randy releases these — informational only.

yellowfin_tuna.narrative: Mix in late June. Peak August (warm water preference, 60+ deg). Sept-Oct strong at canyons. Nov thin.

bigeye_tuna.narrative: Canyon night bite. Peak September. Rare inside 50 nm.

striped_bass.narrative: Spring migration peaks May-Jun (LI Sound). Summer heat lull Jul-Aug except at structure with current (Race, Plum Gut, Block Island Reefs, Montauk holdover). Fall run Sep-Nov (peak Oct).

bluefish.narrative: Peak Jun-Sep. Slug fish at bunker schools.

mahi.narrative: Peak Jul-Aug at high-flyer floats, weedlines, offshore structure.

thresher_shark.narrative: Peak Jun-Aug at Habs Ledge / midshore banks.

mako_shark.narrative: Peak Jun-Aug offshore of Mud Hole / Butterfish Hole. NOTE: mako is now protected — release only.

swordfish.narrative: Canyon deep-drop daytime + night drift. Peak Jul-Sep at Hudson/Block/Atlantis/Veatch. Recovering stock. HMS permit required, keeper >47" LJFL, one fish per angler/day.

wahoo.narrative: Warm-water pelagic. Late summer/fall canyon high-speed troll (14-18 kt). Rides Gulf Stream eddies north. Peak Aug-Oct in warm-water years. Wire leaders mandatory.

sailfish.narrative: Rare NE visitor. Occasional catches at canyons in warmest August water. Not a target species — bycatch on white marlin trolls. Release-only.

white_marlin.narrative: Canyon summer/fall staple. Peak Jul-Sep at Hudson/Block/Atlantis. White Marlin Open in Ocean City every August. Naked ballyhoo on 30w trolling gear. Release-only for most anglers.

blue_marlin.narrative: Deep-canyon apex predator. Less common than white marlin in NE. Peak August at Hudson/Atlantis/Veatch. Big lures, 50-80w tackle. Release-only.

false_albacore.narrative: Fall inshore run — the light-tackle king of Sept-Oct. Blitzes on peanut bunker + silversides at Montauk Point, Block Island, Watch Hill, Race. Not keeper (poor eating) but bucket-list fight.

zones.name: Western Long Island Sound
zones.notes: 30–40+ lb stripers dominating Western Sound (Jul 9, 2026). Live bunker, tube-and-worm, big spoons, night eels all producing. The Angler Fleet (Port Washington) active. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW CT report): Western Sound showing improved consistency with quality bass on deeper structure.

otw.quote: Western Sound showing improved consistency with quality bass on deeper structure.

zones.name: Central Long Island Sound
zones.notes: Deep reef structure holding fish. Morning, evening, overnight bite windows. Tube-and-worm and live eels effective mid-summer. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW CT report): Matt (Black Hall Outfitters) — 'obvious lack of bluefish in the central to eastern Sound'. Sea bass 60+ ft, fluke 40-60 ft.

otw.quote: Better sea bass results coming from 60 feet of water or deeper.

zones.name: The Triangle
zones.notes: Producing 20–30 lb fish with occasional 40 lb specimens (Jul 9, 2026). Solid structure spot.

zones.name: The Race / Race Rock
zones.notes: HOT — 'most consistent bite in Connecticut waters' (Jul 9, 2026). The tide race between Fishers Island and Little Gull, anchored on the west end by Race Rock lighthouse. Structure and current concentrate stripers year-round. Live eels, bucktails, diamond jigs on the drop; best on the tide changes. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW CT report): Capt. Joe Diorio — 'best fishing shallow reefs in 5 to 40 feet of water using live eels', targeting the eastern LI Sound race complex.

otw.quote: Fishing has been solid this week. Striper fishing has been strong, especially overnight.
otw.captain: Matt (Black Hall Outfitters) + Capt. Joe Diorio

zones.name: Plum Gut
zones.notes: The tide race at the east end of Plum Island. Big fish on the drift, especially on the ebb. Diamond jigs, live eels, bucktails.

zones.name: Watch Hill Reef
zones.notes: Reef complex south of Watch Hill. Consistent striper producer. Live bait and tube-and-worm.

zones.name: Millstone Point
zones.notes: Warm-water discharge and structure. Reliable striper spot.

zones.name: Narragansett Bay / Newport Rips
zones.notes: Newport Sportfishing (Capt. Rob Taylor) had a strong holiday weekend. Pamela May Charters, Tall Tailz reporting quality fish. Three-way eels, bucktails, topwater in low light. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW RI report): Dave (Ocean State Tackle) — 'bay is now full of sand eels' and 'still holding squid'. Bass mixed sizes from mouth to Upper Bay.

otw.quote: Bay is now full of sand eels and still holding squid.
otw.captain: Dave (Ocean State Tackle) + Jay (Pamela May Charters)

zones.name: Providence / Seekonk Rivers
zones.notes: Slot to over-slot fish on early morning and dusk shifts (Jul 9, 2026). Topwater and soft plastics.

zones.name: Block Island Reefs (SW Ledge / SE Light)
zones.notes: PRIMARY HOTSPOT — 'large striped bass' 45–48" reported (Jul 9, 2026). RI Kayak Fishing Adventures, Tall Tailz Charters all landing big fish. Live scup, eels, three-ways. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW RI report): Multiple captains confirm — big male 'knotheads mixed in', strong day/night bite. Southwest/Southeast Block going strong; watch for sharks.

otw.quote: Big male knotheads mixed in ... southwest and southeast sides going strong.
otw.captain: Pamela May Charters + Tall Tailz Charters + RIKFA + Ocean State Tackle

zones.name: Montauk Point Rips
zones.notes: 40+ lb bass off Montauk, a notable 60 lb'er landed by Andrew Bernat. 40–80 ft on incoming tide. Live eels and live spot best. Windward Outfitters, Gypsea Charters active. Bite 'beginning to slow' but still productive.

zones.name: Block Island Sound
zones.notes: Transitional water — migratory stripers moved through; residents tide-dependent. Occasional nearshore bluefin push in. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW RI report): Bonito running South County shoreline. Block Island bite strong day + night.

otw.quote: Large slug of bonito that settled in.
otw.captain: Jay (Pamela May Charters) + Dave (Ocean State Tackle)

zones.name: South Shore Long Island (Moriches / Shinnecock)
zones.notes: Rockfish Charters (Capt. Adrian Moeller) jigged bluefin up to 55" — 4 at a time on best day. Trolled smaller bluefin and mahi on midshore trips (Jul 16, 2026).

zones.name: Montauk / East End Offshore
zones.notes: Reel Therapy Charters active. Bluefin moving through, whales/dolphins around; fish 'on the move' in mid-July 2026. Midshore bluefin south of Montauk slowed week's end.

zones.name: Nearshore South of Block Island
zones.notes: HOT ZONE for tuna. Newport Sportfishing (Capt. Rob Taylor, Reel EZ) landed giants here. 'Loads of bait and bluefin, from shorts to giants.' Tall Tailz Charters and multiple RI boats scoring. School bluefin bite building through Jul 2026.

zones.name: The Acid Barge
zones.notes: ~7 mi south of Block Island. Wreck structure holds bait. Mid- to late-summer bluefin, mahi. Slack tide prime.

zones.name: Southeast Coxes Ledge
zones.notes: 80–150+ ft depths. Best on slack tide. Consistent bluefin, occasional yellowfin.

zones.name: The Gully
zones.notes: NE–SW oriented canyon-like feature. Steep banks concentrate baitfish. Bluefin cycle through.

zones.name: Habs Ledge
zones.notes: SW of Montauk Point, 25-fathom curve. 'The 2024 spot of the season.' Bunker and sand eel forage draws tuna and threshers.

zones.name: Tuna Ridge (30-Fathom S of Block)
zones.notes: 30-fathom curve south of Block Island. Contains the Suffolk wreck and other structure. 'Tremendous amount of 30–100lb+ bluefin' along the 20 and 30 fathom lines south of LI — Apex Angling (Capt. Ben Burdine), Jul 2026.

zones.name: The Butterfish Hole
zones.notes: One of the most famous inshore tuna spots. Named for late-70s/early-80s yellowfin feeds on butterfish schools. Still produces. · 2026-08-13: activity spillover — Randy fished 5-13nm east at Coimbra and reported the whole area (Butterfish → Coimbra) is crowded with charter boats.

captain_report.source: Randy Spargo direct (spillover from Coimbra Wreck ~13nm E)

zones.name: The Mud Hole
zones.notes: Deep channel in NY Bight formed by Hudson River flow, depths to 200 ft. Silt/mud bottom draws bait; wrecks throughout. Summer pelagics active.

zones.name: Hudson Canyon
zones.notes: Classic NY canyon. Waypoints: 100 Sq (39°40'N 72°30'W), The Fingers (39°37'N 72°29'W), Tea Cup (39°39'N 72°31'W), The Claw (39°36'N 72°27'W). Yellowfin & bigeye consistent through Jul 2026. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW NJ report — TWO independent sources): Frank Giacalone (Gabriel Tackle Co., Brick) — 'bigeye and yellowfin at the Hudson'. Kyle Tangen (Fishermen's Supply, Point Pleasant Beach) — 'Hudson Canyon has mahi and white marlin'.

otw.quote: Bigeye and yellowfin at the Hudson (Frank Giacalone) + mahi and white marlin (Kyle Tangen)
otw.captain: Frank Giacalone + Kyle Tangen (two independent NJ shops)

zones.name: Block Canyon
zones.notes: Rockfish Charters (Moriches) took 3 yellowfin here on a day trip (mid-Jul 2026). Consistent producer, ~120 mi south of Block Island.

zones.name: Atlantis Canyon
zones.notes: SCORCHING — 'unlimited amount of yellowfin to 80 pounds' on trolled Sterling Tackle bars near West and East Atlantis (Jul 9, 2026). Bigeye showing mid-morning on the banks. West Atlantis ~40°05'N, 70°30'W; East Atlantis ~40°06-08'N, 69°55'W.

zones.name: Veatch / Hydrographer Canyons
zones.notes: Eastern edge of the commonly-fished NE canyon complex. Veatch ~69°35'W, 40°N; Hydrographer 100-fathom ledges ~69°00-05'W, 40°10'N. 130+ mi from LI/RI ports. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW CT report): Capt. Chris Oliver (Keepin' It Reel) — 'We ended up going 12 for 18 on stud yellowfin' plus white marlin action.

otw.quote: We ended up going 12 for 18 on stud yellowfin.

zones.name: 35 Fathom Line (S of Montauk)
zones.notes: Real bathymetric edge — the 35-fathom contour line running south of Montauk. School bluefin follow this edge in summer, yellowfin push here Aug-Sep. Referenced by Kevin Albohn (OTW Bluefin Calendar) as a classic early-season school bluefin edge. User-added spot, awaiting first specific captain report.

zones.name: Long Sand Shoal
zones.notes: 6-mile shoal directly off Old Saybrook / Cornfield Point. Eastern boulder end is the striper zone. Q. Kresser (former River's End Tackle Old Saybrook): 'The eastern end of the shoal is the better area for striped bass fishing.' Literally in Randy's backyard — ~4nm.

zones.name: Six Mile Reef
zones.notes: Glacial boulder ridge 1.5mi off Clinton, 35-45ft with strong rips on the ebb. The Fisherman calls it a 'hotspot of the month' for trolling wireline and parachutes for large stripers. ~7nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Bartlett Reef
zones.notes: Boulder reef off Waterford/Niantic Bay. Big-fish rip fished year after year by Captain Q's Striper Snax and Rock and Roll charters. ~8nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Faulkner's Island Reef
zones.notes: Reef and rip lines around Guilford's lighthouse island. Per Zip06, 'the mid-Sound's most popular island' for striper structure. ~14nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Stratford Shoal / Middle Ground
zones.notes: 3-mile-radius mid-Sound shoal (15-65ft) with lighthouse, hard rocky SE bottom, multiple rip lines. The Fisherman's classic western-Sound trophy zone. ~36nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Point Judith Lighthouse Rip
zones.notes: Where Block Island Sound meets Rhode Island Sound. Classic albie/striper rip. FishingBooker's #1 RI charter town. ~40nm from Old Saybrook. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW RI report): Frances Fleet — 'mix of black sea bass and fluke coming over the rails.'

otw.quote: Mix of black sea bass and fluke coming over the rails.

zones.name: Nebraska Shoal
zones.notes: Plateau rising to 25ft between Point Judith and Charlestown Breachway. The Fisherman notes historical bluefin sightings; Charlestown pond outflow acts as a bait pump. ~36nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Beavertail Point
zones.notes: Jamestown lighthouse point at Narragansett Bay mouth. Steep drop-off, wicked rip on tide changes. Best Fishing in America top-10 RI striper spot. ~45nm from Old Saybrook. Aug 6, 2026 (OTW RI report): Narragansett Bay entrance still producing. Sand eels + squid abundant.

otw.quote: Bay is now full of sand eels.

zones.name: Sakonnet Point / West Island
zones.notes: Historic West Island Fishing Club grounds off Little Compton. Boulder-strewn point with heavy rips. ~54nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Sow and Pigs Reef (Cuttyhunk)
zones.notes: SW tip of Cuttyhunk at Buzzards Bay mouth. The Fisherman's 'surfcaster's paradise' reef, birthplace of American striper fishing (Cuttyhunk Fishing Club, 1865). ~63nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Wasque Rip (Chappaquiddick)
zones.notes: SE tip of Chappaquiddick. Violent rip where Muskeget Channel meets the Atlantic — Vineyard's most famous striper spot, MV Derby staple. ~87nm from Old Saybrook (past Randy's one-way range, but included for visitors with bigger boats).

zones.name: Monomoy Rips / Bearses Shoal
zones.notes: Chatham's shoal complex (Bearses, Stonehorse, Handkerchief, Pollock Rip). Massive tides over 2-10ft sand. Goose Hummock: 'larger tide = more velocity, fish feed most aggressively as current slows toward slack.' ~109nm from Old Saybrook — visitor bucket-list, out of Randy's range.

zones.name: The Coimbra Wreck
zones.notes: Randy fished here 2026-08-13: caught 4 recreational bluefin tuna at 50-55" fork length. Multiple NJ charter boats on scene — confirmed active hotspot. Prior context: WWII tanker torpedoed by U-boat, in 180ft ~30mi SE of Moriches. Per The Fisherman, primary bluefin draw via jigging sand eels, plus threshers/makos June-July and Oct-Nov. ~54nm from Old Saybrook.

captain_report.corroboration: multiple NJ charter boats on scene

zones.name: The Dumping Ground ('The Dump')
zones.notes: 10x10nm box ~30nm SE of Block Island / S of Vineyard. Per On The Water, lacks bottom structure but concentrates fish on contour lines, temp breaks, weed lines. Randy's midshore bluefin sweet spot. ~65-75nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: The Fishtails (Block Canyon N tip)
zones.notes: Randy's 'The Tails' — northern shelf-edge terminus of Block Canyon where bottom drops from ~400ft to 100 fathoms. On The Water: 'The crazy bigeye and tuna chunk bite in Fishtails happened in September 2014 and lasted the bulk of the month.' ~92nm from Old Saybrook — past Randy's one-way range but shown for informational value + visitors with bigger boats.

zones.name: CIA Grounds (Cartwright area, SE of Montauk)
zones.notes: Local named ground SE of Montauk Point mentioned by Capt. Skip (Adios Charters) as a shark/tuna spot paired with the Butterfish Hole area. NorEast Fishing Forum thread 'CIA Grounds and Cartwright' — nickname origin unclear (may derive from initials of a captain, family, or landmark). Randy's buddy reports fish being caught close to shore on the north side of CIA (Aug 28, 2026 text). Estimated position pending confirmed LORAN/GPS numbers.

zones.name: Ranger Wreck (S of Long Island)
zones.notes: Wreck south of Long Island, paired with Coimbra and Habs in the Tight Lines Tackle Aug 24 East End report — 'Fish of various sizes are being encountered around the Coimbra, Habs and Ranger areas, with both soft-plastic and metal jigs producing'. Position estimated pending confirmed coords.

zones.name: Niantic Bay (Black Point / Two Tree Channel)
zones.notes: CT nearshore bay just east of Old Saybrook — includes Black Point, Two Tree Channel, and the Niantic River outflow. The Fisherman CT report Aug 24: 'Black Point, Niantic Bay, and Two Tree Channel have produced a few keeper fluke and sea bass this week... Striped bass fishing continues to be best around the reefs at first light and after dark.' Randy's backyard. 5nm from Old Saybrook.

zones.name: Cornfield Point (Old Saybrook mouth)
zones.notes: Old Saybrook headland at the western mouth of the Connecticut River — Randy's home port entrance. Rocky point with strong tidal current, produces stripers year-round on live eels and bucktails. Q. Kresser (former Rivers End Tackle Old Saybrook, per Long Sand Shoal note): 'The eastern end of the shoal is the better area for striped bass fishing.' Cornfield Point marks the western end.

zones.name: Fishers Island (south side reefs)
zones.notes: South side of Fishers Island — reef and rip system between Watch Hill Reef and the eastern end of Fishers Island. The Fisherman RI report Aug 24: 'nice-sized striped bass being caught from the Watch Hill Reefs and along the south side of Fishers Island. There have been a few bluefish around as well.' Complements The Race zone (which covers the tide race between Fishers Island and Little Gull).

zones.name: Buzzards Bay
zones.notes: Big Massachusetts back-bay complex between Cape Cod and Rhode Island. Striper + blues year-round; false albacore fall run. Surfaced 2026-08-30 via spot_discovery from 3 different captain sources (OTW Media, Fisherman Magazine, My Fishing Cape Cod).

zones.name: Cape Cod Bay
zones.notes: MA Cape Cod Bay — striper + bluefish + summer bluefin. Major migration corridor + late-summer bluefin destination. Surfaced 2026-08-30 via spot_discovery (My Fishing Cape Cod + Fisherman Magazine).
